review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read the upstream definitions it uses: Tensor, stageLeading, rawPoolLeading, maskedPoolCode, poolEnumeration, Execution and Stage. The ℂ commitment is pervasive upstream: Execution, Stage, kernel, stageLeading and rawPoolLeading are all hard-coded to ℂ. So generalising the Stage/Execution theorems (`exists_rawPoolStage`, `exists_actualPoolStage`) would need a large refactor outside this file, and I did not report them. The only local, cheap generalisation is the 0/1-indicator `decodedLeading`, and it is only useful if `stageLeading` and `rawPoolLeading` are generalised too. I did not report the derivable `positive` binder in `decodePool_eq_iff`, since dropping a binder is out of scope. The remaining declarations are combinatorial and already general in the label and prefix types. Remaining uncertainty: I did not check how many downstream users depend on the ℂ instantiation of `rawPoolLeading` or `decodedLeading`.

findings.problem: `decodedLeading` is a pure 0/1 indicator tensor, and its comparison lemma with `rawPoolLeading` only unfolds `if … then 1 else 0` and rewrites the guard propositions. Nothing uses any property of ℂ. Both are pinned to ℂ because `stageLeading` and `rawPoolLeading` (upstream) are ℂ-valued. `Tensor K X Y Z` is just `X → Y → Z → K`, so the ℂ commitment is not needed here.
findings.proposed_change: Generalise the indicator pattern. Make `stageLeading` and `rawPoolLeading` take `{K : Type*} [Zero K] [One K]`, so the result is `Tensor K …`. Make `decodedLeading` take the same `{K} [Zero K] [One K]`. Restate `rawPoolLeading_eq_decodedLeading` for `(rawPoolLeading … : Tensor K …)`. The proof should go through unchanged: `unfold … ; simp only [hx, hy]; congr 1; apply propext` never inspects K. The existing ℂ uses become the instance `K := ℂ`. If the upstream refactor is not wanted, at least state `decodedLeading` for a general `[Zero K] [One K]` so the indicator is not tied to ℂ.
findings.benefit: The decode-by-pool characterisation of the leading tensor becomes reusable over any coefficient type, such as other fields or ℤ. The fact that the proof is purely combinatorial becomes visible in the statement, and the ℂ-specific definitions no longer hide the field-independent content.
